options.text: FlashAttention approximates the attention output; the paper reports lower accuracy than standard attention on long-context tasks, so it should be avoided when numerical fidelity matters.
FlashAttention v1's speedup over naive attention comes entirely from replacing the softmax with a cheaper approximation (piecewise-linear exp), not from IO-awareness or tiling.

By processing K/V in tiles and rescaling the running `(m, l, acc)` triple via the online-softmax recurrence, FlashAttention avoids ever materializing the [S, S] score matrix in HBM, reducing HBM traffic from O(S^2) to O(S).

The rescale factor `exp(m_i - m_new)` on `acc` is required because `acc` was previously anchored at `m_i`; the update aligns it to the new anchor `m_new` before adding the new tile's contribution, preserving exact algebra.

explanation: Options C, D are correct; options A, B are incorrect. A (Wrong): FlashAttention is exact, not approximate. B (Wrong): no cheap-exp approximation is involved. C (Correct): tiled + online softmax + fused → O(S) HBM traffic. D (Correct): `exp(m_i - m_new)` rescale is the exact-algebra alignment.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: FlashAttention is exact, not approximate.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: no cheap-exp approximation is involved.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: tiled + online softmax + fused → O(S) HBM traffic.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: `exp(m_i - m_new)` rescale is the exact-algebra alignment.

assumptions: FlashAttention-forward as documented in the original paper (v1).
SMEM sufficient for tiled Q/K/V blocks.
nonImplications: Does not imply FlashAttention wins for every shape (very small S may not benefit).
Does not imply v1/v2/v3 have identical implementations; scheduling and Hopper-specific optimizations differ.

distractorRationales.A: Confuses IO-aware exact algorithm with approximation.
distractorRationales.B: Fabricates a cheap-exp story for the speedup.
